questions.q: Class B concrete is the usual spec for:
o: Slabs on fill and non-bearing walls
questions.n: Class B (1:2.5:5) suits lightly loaded elements.

questions.q: For construction sand, the ideal grading is:
questions.n: A range of sizes packs densely.

questions.q: Ready-mixed concrete is ordered by:
questions.n: Ready-mix is batched and billed by volume.

questions.q: Concrete stiffens suddenly soon after mixing, but regains plasticity when remixed without extra water. This is:
questions.n: False set comes from gypsum and remixing fixes it; flash set is permanent.

questions.q: Gravel commonly specified for slabs on grade and slabs on fill is:
questions.n: 3/4" gravel is the usual coarse aggregate for slabs.

questions.q: The nominal maximum coarse aggregate size is limited to:
o: 3/4 of the minimum clear spacing between bars
questions.n: Also 1/5 of form width and 1/3 of slab depth.

questions.q: The biggest single factor in concrete strength is the:
questions.n: Abrams' law: strength falls as w/c rises.

questions.q: To make concrete stronger and more durable, the water–cement ratio should be:
questions.n: Less excess water means less porosity, so strength and durability go up.

questions.q: The most dependable way to consolidate concrete in forms is a:
questions.n: Internal vibration removes entrapped air.

questions.q: Which ingredient makes up roughly 60–80% of a concrete mix's volume and keeps cost down?
questions.n: Aggregates are the bulk filler; cement is the costly binder.

questions.q: Concrete's defining structural strength is:
questions.n: It's strong in compression and weak in tension.

questions.q: Typical form-stripping times: walls, columns and beam sides come off in...
questions.n: Vertical faces carry no weight and can be stripped early.

questions.q: Props under beams and arches spanning more than 6 m stay for about:
questions.n: Up to 6 m: 14 days; over 6 m: 21 days.

questions.q: White or gray powdery salts appear on a masonry wall after rains. This is called:
questions.n: Water carries soluble salts to the surface, where they dry into efflorescence.

questions.q: Normal-weight concrete weighs about:
questions.n: About 23.5 kN/m³.

questions.q: Concrete samples from a ready-mix truck should be taken from:
questions.n: The middle portion best represents the batch.

questions.q: To make lightweight concrete, add:
questions.n: Perlite is a light expanded aggregate.

questions.q: Cement, aggregates and water with no reinforcement at all make ______ concrete.
questions.n: Unreinforced concrete is called plain concrete.

questions.q: Which cement hardens very fast and gains strength quickly, but generates too much heat for mass concrete?
questions.n: High alumina cement is rapid-hardening, and its heat of hydration rules out mass pours.

questions.q: Foot traffic on a new slab is usually allowed after about:
questions.n: Light foot traffic is fine after a day or two; loads wait longer.

questions.q: As the water–cement ratio rises, ______ falls.
questions.n: More water makes the paste weaker and more porous.

questions.q: Piles, marine works and water-retaining walls exposed to chlorides and sulfates benefit from a cement that keeps gaining strength for years. Which?
questions.n: Slag cement improves impermeability and chemical resistance and gains strength long after 28 days.

questions.q: In very hot weather with ordinary Portland cement and no early loads, column forms on a fast-track job can usually come off after:
questions.n: Vertical forms carry no load; in hot weather 24 hours is typical.

questions.q: Props under a slab spanning more than 4.5 m stay in place for about:
questions.n: Up to 4.5 m: 7 days; over 4.5 m: 14 days.

questions.q: Which cement is characterized by slow hardening?
questions.n: Pozzolanic reactions are slow, so early strength gain is slower.

questions.q: Match the gravel designation to its size range: G 3/4 is about...
questions.n: G 3/4 covers roughly 10–20 mm; G 3/8 is about 6–10 mm.

questions.q: Typical stripping time for slab soffit forms (props left in place):
questions.n: Slab soffits come off around 3 days with props retained.

questions.q: How easily fresh concrete can be placed, consolidated and finished without segregating is its:
questions.n: Slump is the field test.
